title: Choose the visual direction
question: Choose a direction for the dashboard redesign. The screen remains a working product, and all measurements stay clearly simulated. Three other catalog forms remain available for a fresh hand.

options.label: Nocturne Survey Atlas
options.lineage: Bathymetric survey charts and contemporary scientific atlases
options.thesis: A dark survey language gives measured trends a distinctive visual signature without pretending nodes have geographic relationships.
options.viewport: A compact product header leads into Monitored nodes, the existing search and status filter, and three readable node cards; restrained contour lines frame the cards and return as quiet chart guides on the detail screen.
options.risk: Contour marks could imply geography or hidden topology; keep them decorative, low-contrast, and never connect one node to another.

raised.raise: Use a deliberate semantic type scale and tabular numerals so hierarchy and measurement values remain distinct.
Pair every product claim with visible interface evidence and keep the simulated-data label beside the inventory.
Use a consistent visual legend and explicit text labels so status is never communicated by color alone.

options.label: Applied Research Journal
options.lineage: Engineering journal figures and field-research reports
options.thesis: A carefully edited research surface lets people scan node health first and inspect the evidence behind each measurement.
options.viewport: A restrained top bar leads into a concise node roster with clear status, identity, location, and timestamps; the detail page aligns real chart units and values with a narrow annotation rule.
options.risk: The safer editorial language can feel like a familiar admin dashboard if the annotation discipline is too timid.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: Typography becomes an expressive system whose changing axes transform a complete glyph specimen.
options.viewport: A display glyph dominates above a grid of characters and a live axis readout.
options.risk: A type specimen asks visitors to inspect lettering instead of network-node health.
options.case: Declined on both axes: the audience arrives to inspect node status and measurements, not manipulate font axes; the specimen structure obscures the working product.
options.kept: Typography should still behave as a system: use clear label/value hierarchy and tabular numerals for measurements.

options.label: Monochrome Product Proof
options.thesis: Each statement is paired with a product detail that makes the claim visible and testable.
options.viewport: A single product claim sits beside an interface proof and becomes a vertical sequence of claim-and-evidence pairs.
options.risk: Marketing-page pacing can make a working operations dashboard feel like a promotional landing page.
options.case: Declined on both axes: a marketing narrative does not match the operator's scan-and-compare task and would displace the existing inventory workflow.
options.kept: Keep every statement honest and visibly grounded in the actual fixture-backed interface.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A precise color and symbol legend makes a route readable across varied terrain.
options.viewport: A mapped terrain is overlaid with a numbered route, paired controls, and a compact symbol legend.
options.risk: Route and terrain graphics could falsely imply geographic locations or network topology that the product does not contain.
options.case: Declined on both axes: the map's central route has no real counterpart in the fixture data, while the resulting map would replace rather than clarify the dashboard.
options.kept: Carry over the discipline of a consistent legend and explicit labels for every state and measurement.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar dark operations dashboard uses a clean grid, restrained accent color, and conventional cards to keep node status and metrics immediately legible.
canonCard.viewport: A compact header and standard search/filter controls lead into a simple node grid with explicit status labels.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to understand but offers less visual distinction for a portfolio presentation.
